int_name: N ETTING ST & W STILES ST

result.summary: The image shows a residential sidewalk that is significantly narrowed by physical obstructions, including a large metal planter, a trash bin, and cardboard boxes. While a paved walkway exists, these items create a constrained environment for pedestrians and impede accessibility. The absence of the roadway in the frame prevents a complete assessment of traffic-related risks or crossing infrastructure.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: A large metal planter and a blue trash bin are placed directly on the sidewalk, significantly reducing the usable width for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Tripping Hazards and Clutter
hazards.description: Cardboard boxes and miscellaneous items are scattered near the base of the stairs, creating potential trip hazards and further narrowing the path.

interventions.title: Clear Sidewalk Path
interventions.description: Relocate large planters, trash bins, and private storage items to ensure a continuous, unobstructed clear width for all pedestrians, including those using mobility aids.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Management Policy
interventions.description: Implement and enforce local ordinances that require property owners to keep the public right-of-way clear of private property and debris.

result.summary: The environment is a narrow residential street characterized by a lack of dedicated, unobstructed pedestrian space. The existing narrow walkway on the left is heavily blocked by trash receptacles and architectural features, forcing pedestrians into the travel lane shared with vehicles.

hazards.name: Walkway Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash cans, planters, and stairs significantly block the narrow paved area on the left, forcing pedestrians into the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Separation
hazards.description: No clear, protected, or continuous space for pedestrians exists, requiring them to share a narrow roadway with moving and parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and building corners create blind spots for pedestrians entering the roadway from between cars or buildings.

interventions.title: Obstruction Removal
interventions.description: Enforce clear walkway zones by relocating trash bins and managing private property encroachments on the public right-of-way.

interventions.title: Shared Street (Woonerf) Treatment
interventions.description: Formalize the street as a pedestrian-priority shared space using distinct paving, signage, and traffic calming to slow vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install lower-height, more frequent lighting to improve visibility and security for pedestrians at night.

result.summary: The image depicts a narrow residential alleyway or side street lacking formal pedestrian infrastructure such as sidewalks or marked crossings. The ground surface is severely degraded, consisting of dirt, gravel, and broken asphalt, which poses significant accessibility and safety challenges.

hazards.name: Unpaved and Degraded Surface
hazards.description: The ground is uneven with loose gravel and dirt, creating trip hazards and making it inaccessible for wheelchairs or strollers.

hazards.name: Blind Corner
hazards.description: The building on the left creates a sharp blind corner where pedestrians and vehicles might collide without warning.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image at the building corner.

hazards.name: Walkway Obstructions
hazards.description: Trash bins and utility equipment narrow the usable space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pave and Formalize Walkway
interventions.description: Install a level, paved sidewalk or shared-space surface to improve accessibility and safety.

interventions.title: Improve Street Lighting
interventions.description: Add pedestrian-scale lighting to ensure visibility and safety during night hours.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming and Signage
interventions.description: Install 'Slow' or 'Pedestrian Zone' signage to alert drivers to the shared nature of the space.

result.summary: The image shows a narrow, one-way residential street with row houses and narrow sidewalks. While the narrow geometry likely encourages low vehicle speeds, the environment lacks basic pedestrian infrastructure like marked crosswalks and curb ramps, and the sidewalks are obstructed by utility poles and trash bins.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: A utility pole, trash can, and planters block the narrow sidewalk, forcing pedestrians into the street.

hazards.name: Lack of Curb Ramps
hazards.description: The absence of curb ramps at the intersection creates a significant barrier for individuals with mobility impairments.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at the intersection to meet accessibility standards.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Apply continental or ladder-style pavement markings to define the pedestrian crossing area.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Clear Zone
interventions.description: Establish and enforce a clear walking path by relocating trash receptacles and managing private planters.
